newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler - EMU criteria must be fulfilled clearly.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler - EMU criteria must be fulfilled clearly.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Tuesday urged clear and credible fulfilment of the convergence criteria required to take part in the planned launch of the Euro in January 1999.

In a speech delivered at an engineering industry conference in Turin, Zeitler said a stability pact, as has been suggested by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, was essential to ensure that single currency member states kept their finances in order once the Euro was introduced.
"But even a stability pact should not deflect from a clear and credible fulfilment of budgetary criteria in particular at entry to the currency union," he said.
A copy of Zeitler's speech was made available in Frankfurt in advance.
Zeitler also stressed the need for a stable Euro, warning that any weakening of the common currency would damage the union in the eyes of the public and the markets.

Doubts about the Euro's stability could prompt a shift of capital out of the countries most likely to participate in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the start, pushing up interest rates and thus harming companies.

"One must not overlook the fact that monetary capital formation is relatively weak; many investors have short-term positions and are thus armed and ready to react immediately to signs of a weak Euro," Zeitler said.
